newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH KOMERCNI SURGES ON FOREIGN DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: CZECH KOMERCNI SURGES ON FOREIGN DEMAND.

text.p: Shares in the largest Czech commercial bank, Komercni Banka a.s. surged on Wednesday, up roughly five percent midway through the Prague Stock Exchange's continuous trading session.

Komercni shares rose 135 crowns after the morning price fixing to 2,840 crowns at mid session, on mostly foreign demand dealers said, boosting the RPIX index of 11 shares 15.2 points from the fixing to 1,303.8.
Dealers said the stock was racing to catch up with Komercni's Global Depositary Receipts (GDR) which are trading in London at a large premium.
"The price is copying the development of the GDRs in London. The standard discount is about 300 crowns," said Tomas Michalek, a broker with Raiffeisen Capital & Investment.
Komercni GDRs were quoted at the equvivalent of 3,487 crowns in London at 1225 GMT.
Komercni has risen some 30 percent since the beginning of the year, which dealers attribute to demand from foreign portfolio investors. The GDRs in London rose by over 50 percent in the same period.
The turnover in Komercni was moderate in the first half of the continuous trading was 4.4 million crowns.
"(Komercni's) performance hasn't changed, but foreign portfolio managaers are buying. There are very few shares (being offered)," said Michalek.
